So voat. I feel like an idiot. I posted back in June about having trouble losing weight and getting migraines after I worked out. A lot of people suggested it was my age (i'm not in college anymore), the speed with which I was trying to change my body, etc. etc.

Well, the migraines got worse and they started to stay there all day. I went to a doctor and he started running a bunch of tests (Cat scan, etc) and things were coming back normal. AT some point I was hunting around online doing some homework on migraines and I stumbled upon some posts that mentioned Taurine supplementation being very very effective for some people. Now keep in mind at this point the headaches were getting so bad that I was missing work and that when I did go in, people thought my speech was slurred, and it looked like someone had punched my right eye (deep circles around it). I should also point out, the headaches/migraines were only on the left side of my head behind my eye.

Well, I tried the taurine and it turned the pain down... nearly completely gone ... for about five hours to six hours. Taurine is a semi essential amino acid. Your body produces some, but not all of the amount it needs. I discovered pretty quickly my body was basically normal as long as I kept supplementing with taurine every six hours or so. Irritating, but it was making me more functional. Well here's where it gets interesting. One day I happened to be thinking, "Gee I wonder what could cause me to have a Taurine deficiency"... and started hunting around.

It turns out that Alanine supplementation is theorized to possibly cause deficiency in long term dosages. It competes with Taurine for transportation sites in the body. They compete for for absorption in the intestines and for reabsorption from the kidneys. Alanine and Taurine seem to have a very interesting balance in the cell.. they are both regulated by similar pathways, contain sulfur, and are connected with different forms of exercise tolerance. Alanine improves your muscle endurance in the 60-240 second range, Taurine changes your adaptations to distance and marathon running. Taurine helps control the flow ions in and out of the cell... basically electrolytes and minerals find it much easier to reach equilibrium with adequate taurine. You also need Taurine to digest fats (bile salts) and to absorb fat related vitamins. Taurine is the most abundant amino acid in the eyes, heart, and brain, but you don't make proteins out of it. It also functions as a neurotransmitter. No human studies have been done past a few weeks on alanine supplementation (despite the fact that it is in TONS of products now), but there's a lot of good evidence that it could become a long term problem for some people. Well, thats fine i though. I'm not taking alanine!

Oh but I was wrong. Several days later I happened to look down at the protein supplement I was taking. And was surprised to find ... alanine. 1.4 g per scoop. I was taking 2-3 scoops per day, for about five years. Also, it contains another amino acid called serine, which helps to convert taurine to alanine in nerve cells.

Electrolyte balance is central to most of the theories on migraines (cortical spreading depression).

I've stopped using the protein supplement. Three weeks later (about the time it takes for Alanine levels to return to normal) my body seems more like it did in college. I can run farther and faster than I could a month ago, and I don't feel like I should be put in a nursing home (@33 yrs old).

I just wanted share this info and let people know that they should cycle these supplements. I think one of the problems was that I had been taking a sulfure containing cystein supplement, and when I stopped that probably killed off the last of the Taurine my body was holding onto.

Taurine is interestingly in a lot of energy drinks, but none of the protein supplements i used to take.

You want my advice? Stop eating all that shit.

Eat meat, and occasionally liver and heart meat to get the extras. Maybe throw in some natto.
